note: Starby real-run checks. Every entry is a run we did ourselves on a clean GitHub Actions runner (2 vCPU, no secrets) with the repo's own README usage. kind: daily = picked from trending by us; commissioned = requested by the maintainer (the verdict is not for sale). Contact: starby.verify@gmail.com

items.task: Turn a demo shop page into text (markdown) an AI agent can read
result: Product name, price ($244.99) and details came out as clean markdown
Same page, same runner, median of 3: Lightpanda 0.27 s / 22 MB vs headless Chrome 1.94 s / 430 MB (PSS)
items.catch: Pages that load products late need --wait-until networkidle (--wait-ms 3000 still showed Loading). Telemetry is on by default.

items.task: Give the model 400 real 5-minute price candles and ask for the next 120
items.ran: README predictor example, Kronos-small + Kronos-Tokenizer-base, CPU only, same call with seeds 0-4
result: All 5 forecasts said down (137.9-141.2); the real price went up, 153.6 to 161.6
About 51 s per forecast on CPU, average error 7.4-8.1%
items.catch: One test set cannot judge the whole model. Not financial advice. No commits in the 90 days before the run.

items.task: Let an AI operate a real desktop app: calculate 7 x 8 in gnome-calculator
items.ran: README commands against gnome-calculator on a virtual Linux desktop
result: The app showed 56
0 mouse moves: it worked through the accessibility tree, not screen pixels
items.catch: Needed a window manager (openbox) on the runner.

items.task: Crawl a whole quotes site with the README spider
result: 100 quotes saved from 10 pages
Median about 1 second for the whole crawl

items.task: Give 3 AI agents their own folder on one repo
items.ran: wt switch --create (x3), wt list, wt merge main, wt remove (wt v0.81.0)
result: 3 branches and 3 worktree folders from 3 commands (28 characters vs 71 with plain git)
wt merge main merged and removed the folder; wt remove refused a folder with an unsaved file
items.catch: Without wt config shell install it cannot change your directory.

items.task: Run a large language model on a small machine with no GPU
result: 13.6 GB model file ran with 1.8 GB peak RAM on 2 cores, no GPU

items.task: Run AWS services locally without an AWS account
items.ran: README quick start, compared with LocalStack latest on the same runner
result: Floci was ready in 0.09 s
LocalStack latest exited with code 55 (it now needs a token)

items.task: Install every skill into a fresh Claude Code project
items.ran: npx skills@latest add mattpocock/skills -a claude-code --skill '*' -y (3 fresh projects)
result: 38 skills installed, median 1.39 s
103 files: 99 text (markdown/yaml), 4 code
items.catch: Using the skills needs an agent and a model; that part was not run. Pick the plugin or skills.sh, not both.

items.task: Make a project agent-ready with Spec Kit
items.ran: README install, then the one setup command
result: One command in 0.39 s created 29 files
items.catch: Agent folders may hold tokens: add them to .gitignore.

items.task: Install gstack, then test its /careful guard with risky commands an agent might run
items.ran: README install step 1 (git clone ... ~/.claude/skills/gstack && ./setup), then the careful hook with 8 commands in a small repo
result: Setup finished (exit 0) and added 66 skills in 175 s on 2 cores
2 of 8 commands blocked (force-push to main, rm -rf ~), 4 asked first, 2 allowed; 0.14 s per check
items.catch: /careful is per session: type it each time. Needs Bun. README says 31 s setup on 4 cores; ours took about 3 minutes.

items.task: Test a small todo app (with one planted bug) the way an agent would
items.ran: README install and quick start, then open / snapshot -i / fill / click / errors on the todo app
result: Refs found the textbox and buttons; the added item showed up on re-read
Clear done left the item, and errors --json named the bug (ReferenceError: doneItems is not defined); 0.016 s per page read
items.catch: On Ubuntu 26.04 Chrome would not start (no usable sandbox) until unprivileged user namespaces were allowed.

items.task: Check pages for the tells that make a site look AI-made
items.ran: README install (npx skills add nutlope/hallmark -g), then sloplint on three pages
result: Its AI-slop test page: 24 FAIL in 0.12 s; its example page: 0
Our own site: 24 FAIL, 21 of them colour codes outside the palette
items.catch: No release yet and few contributors for its stars. skills.sh rated it Med Risk at install.

items.task: Clean up a small todo app full of typical AI-code leftovers, and compare speed with Flake8
items.ran: README commands (uvx ruff@0.17.4 check, ruff check --fix, ruff format) on the app; ruff vs flake8 on CPython 3.14 Lib/, default rules, 3 runs each
result: 13 problems found in 0.024 s; --fix fixed 7, and one warning left (response never used) pointed at a real typo bug
CPython Lib (1,830 files): Flake8 91.6 s vs Ruff 0.98 s, about 94x faster
items.catch: Default rules are light: == None passed and the misspelled name was not flagged directly (a star import hid it). Turn on more rules.

items.task: Watch a small todo API and alert when it fails or goes down
items.ran: README release binary v3.16.0, a /metrics page via prometheus-client, two alert rules (up == 0 for 15s, errors > 5%); a bug switched on, then the app killed 3 times
result: Error alert firing 21.3 s after 1 in 5 todo requests started failing
Down alert firing 21.8 s after the app was killed (median of 3; 15 s of it is the for: wait)
items.catch: Prometheus only flags alerts; a phone or chat message needs Alertmanager.

items.task: Add a design system to a fresh React todo app and let it pick the page for an agent
items.ran: README install (@astryxdesign/core, theme-neutral, stylex, cli 0.7.11), npx astryx init, astryx build "todo list app with tasks and due dates", astryx template, README Vite setup, vite build, astryx doctor --built
result: init wrote 35 lines of agent rules into AGENTS.md in 0.66 s (start from a template, no raw div, no raw hex/px)
build picked a template; the 1,218-line page built first try with 0 type errors and 0 raw divs; doctor 12 pass, 0 fail
items.catch: At 430 px phone width the task-title column disappeared and the right columns were cut off. Beta, React 19+ only.
